message: The study contract is locked for planner handoff. Use the 22 June to 27 June window, keep the 27 June 2:00 PM cutoff hard, and preserve the time blocks and subject priorities shown below.

goal.title: Mid-week revision sprint before 27 June assessment block

study_scope.subject: Mathematics
study_scope.intent: High-weight formula application and mixed-problem practice before the 27 June assessment.

study_scope.subject: Mathematics
study_scope.intent: Backlog-grounded revision with sequence pattern recognition and direct problem-solving.

study_scope.subject: Science
study_scope.intent: Concept repair plus labelled-diagram recall for nervous system and hormones.

study_scope.subject: Science
study_scope.intent: Numerical practice and ray-diagram correction with emphasis on sign convention.

study_scope.subject: Social Science
study_scope.intent: Source-based revision, timeline recall, and map-linked retention.

study_scope.subject: Social Science
study_scope.intent: Selective revision of soil/resource classification and one-cycle map recap.

planning_notes: This intake is intentionally complex and planner-ready.
Respect the hard deadline on 27 June at 2:00 PM local time.
Keep the final day light: recall, formulas, and confidence-preserving review only.
Treat daily_study_hours as already negotiated realistic study capacity.
Do not schedule before 06:45 on normal days or after 23:15.
Prefer Mathematics and Science in the first half of the window; keep lighter Social Science recap closer to the deadline.
Use remaining_subtopics aggressively for sequencing because they reflect actual weak or pending work.
Avoid stacking two heavy numerical blocks back-to-back without a concept or recall buffer.
The student performs better with finishable sessions and visible progress, so the planner should avoid fragmented micro-sessions.
If feasibility becomes tight, reduce the depth of Resources and Development before cutting core Maths or Science study items.

study_items.subject: Mathematics
study_items.reason: Highest-value Maths chapter in this window, combining formula recall weakness with substantial mixed-problem practice demand.
planning_notes: Do this early in the window.
Mix formula recall with cone-cylinder-frustum application sets.
End with mixed word problems rather than only direct formula substitution.

study_items.subject: Mathematics
study_items.reason: Secondary Maths chapter with moderate backlog, mainly around nth-term interpretation and sum-based direct questions.
planning_notes: Keep this practice-first.
Use quick solved examples, then shift to independent questions.
Good candidate for a medium-energy slot.

study_items.subject: Science
study_items.reason: Concept-heavy chapter with known recall gaps in neuron flow, reflex arc, and endocrine mapping, so it needs both understanding and memory reinforcement.
planning_notes: Use labelled-diagram recall and oral self-explanation.
Break the chapter into nervous system, plant movement, and hormones.
Do not keep this too late at night because retention quality drops.

study_items.subject: Science
study_items.reason: Needs targeted numerical correction and ray-diagram accuracy rather than full chapter relearning.
planning_notes: Pair numericals with sign-convention correction.
Use one short formula sheet refresh before problem sets.
Place before the final day so numericals are not rushed.

study_items.subject: Social Science
study_items.reason: Important theory chapter, but the learner mainly needs source recall, event sequencing, and concise retention rather than long reading.
planning_notes: Keep it recap-heavy and writing-light.
Use one timeline pass and one source recall pass.
Best suited to lower-energy evening or post-Maths recovery slots.

study_items.subject: Social Science
study_items.reason: Lower-priority selective revision item included for breadth, mostly to avoid a completely untouched chapter in the assessment block.
planning_notes: Keep this shortest and easiest to cut if time pressure rises.
Focus on soil types, resource classification, and one map pass.
Do not over-read the textbook here.
